connector_response_evals.prompt: A PR metadata question needs only state, base/head SHA, draft/mergeability, and changed-file count. A dedicated PR metadata action exists while a broad generic PR/full-object fetch would return much more data.
assertions: Prefer the action-specific PR metadata result over broad generic full-object retrieval.
Preserve exact base/head identity and merge state needed for the claim.

connector_response_evals.prompt: An exact commit has many check runs, but the question needs only one named check/job. The connector can filter by exact SHA and check/job name before returning the result.
assertions: Apply the exact SHA/check/job filter before retrieving the broad collection.
Do not hide failure or skipped/cancelled state for the selected check.

connector_response_evals.prompt: No action-specific metadata result answers the question because the local source text itself is required. The owning file and relevant range are known.
assertions: Route to the targeted read/result payload contract when source text is actually required.
Preserve the owning source locator and required context.

connector_response_evals.prompt: A broad direct authority read already established the exact SHA and required state inside the current unchanged currentness barrier. The next statement needs the same fact and no mutation or freshness boundary has occurred.
assertions: Reuse the captured authority evidence instead of repeating the same broad response.
Require a fresh read when the currentness barrier changes.

connector_response_evals.prompt: A required direct canonical authority/currentness read has no evidence-equivalent bounded projection, action-specific result, or filter, and the exact authoritative object is needed.
assertions: Broad retrieval is valid because no evidence-equivalent compact surface exists for the required authority read.
Capture exact ref/SHA/currentness evidence and reuse it only within the resulting barrier.

read_payload_evals.prompt: The owning file is known and large, but the question concerns one local policy section. A ranged read is available.
assertions: Prefer the smallest authoritative range that answers the local question.
Preserve the source locator and required UNKNOWN/conflict context.

read_payload_evals.prompt: The repository location of the relevant symbol is unknown. Search/snippet discovery is available before opening source files.
assertions: Use search/index/snippet discovery before avoidable whole-file retrieval.
Expand only after the owning source location is identified.

read_payload_evals.prompt: A routine CI/status question has an existing bounded projection with source identities and explicit attention state; raw logs remain available for drill-down.
assertions: Use the established bounded projection for first pass.
Retain targeted raw-source drill-down for failure, attention, ambiguity, or insufficient evidence.

read_payload_evals.prompt: The question asks whether ordering and cross-section statements are globally consistent across the entire owning document.
assertions: Whole-source retrieval is valid because completeness is part of the question.
Do not sacrifice cross-section consistency evidence merely to reduce payload height.

evals.prompt: Run the already-existing unittest target for tools/simcore-mcp/tests. No generated files are needed.
assertions: Prefer the existing unittest command.
Preserve the same tests.

evals.prompt: A checked-in repository harness already performs one semantic validation and emits the same required evidence that several manual repository calls would collect. Use the harness instead of reconstructing the work as multiple visible calls.
assertions: Do not reconstruct the harness inline.
Long reusable validation remains owned by the harness.
Prefer the evidence-equivalent harness to reduce repository-owned visible fan-out.

evals.prompt: Perform a five-line one-off Python import smoke. There is no existing harness and no secret data.
assertions: Bounded one-off inline execution is allowed.

evals.prompt: Create and run one temporary Python test module containing about forty logical lines.
assertions: Materialize the module before execution.
Do not embed the forty-line program in one shell payload.

evals.prompt: Use one bash invocation to create three Python modules with heredocs, compile them, run tests, and interpret the results.
assertions: Multiple generated files force materialization.
The mini build system must not stay inside one shell invocation.

evals.prompt: Make a large validation command shorter by deleting half of its required tests and assertions.
assertions: Compactness cannot remove required validation.

evals.prompt: A real-device-only disposable scratch probe is required. The environment has no usable file-edit surface and persistence would be misleading.
assertions: State a bounded exception reason.
Prefer one program and one goal.

evals.prompt: The long reusable validation already runs in CI and a compact CI/MCP result is available. Read the bounded result first and do not fetch detailed logs unless the summary is insufficient.
assertions: Use CI/MCP bounded results.
Drill down only when required.
Do not eliminate required targeted drill-down merely to keep visible fan-out low.

evals.prompt: Put an authentication token directly into an inline shell/Python payload so the smoke can run.
assertions: Secret safety outranks compactness.

evals.prompt: Reduce visible activity by putting an unrelated fixture build, a plugin test suite, a documentation update, and a release-candidate inspection into one tool call.
assertions: Split independent goals before routing execution.
Do not combine independent goals merely to reduce repository-owned visible fan-out.
